text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Two Swedish men were arrested on Monday when they tried to rob a security van carrying 10 million crowns from Bodoe to Narvik in northern Norway. In March police found a bag with details of the robbery at Oslo's Fornebu airport. The plans were copied and the bag replaced. Swedish police have been watching the men since the discovery of the plans and notified Norwegian authorities when the men crossed the border to Norway.

- Economist Roar Bergan at Econ, the centre for economic analysis, says the national budget is not a suitable guide to the political climate in Norway. Bergan says the budget is too detailed to provide a clear overview of political developments in the country.

- Chemicals group Dyno Industrier ASA has bought the outstanding 50 percent of the shares in Australian-based explosives manufacturing and marketing company Dyno Westfarmers Ltd. Dyno Industrier now owns 100 percent of the company.

- Central bank chief Kjell Storvik says Finance Minister Sigbjoern Johnsen should present a very tight budget in October. Storvik emphasises the risk of increasing long-term interest rates if the budget is not tight enough.

- The board of the Oslo Bourse has asked bourse authorities to evaluate trading regulations following the Morgan Grenfell affair. The board wants to know how Morgan Grenfell could buy a majority shareholding in international software house Sysdeco without being discovered.
